title: Coherent approximation for a flat Noetherian scheme groupoid
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $(U,R,s,t,c,e,i)$ be a groupoid in schemes over $S$ [def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws]. A quasi-coherent module on this groupoid is a pair $(M,\alpha)$ with $M$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module [pqf-def-coherent] and an isomorphism $\alpha:t^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}s^*M$ [def-pc-module-pullback], whose pullback by $e$ is the identity and whose pullbacks to composable pairs satisfy $c^*\alpha=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\alpha\circ\operatorname{pr}_0^*\alpha$ under the canonical pullback identifications. Morphisms $f:(M,\alpha)\to(N,\beta)$ are module maps satisfying $s^*f\circ\alpha=\beta\circ t^*f$. Such a module is coherent when $M$ is coherent. Assume $U,R$ are Noetherian schemes, meaning quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Assume $s,t$ are flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], quasi-compact (inverse images of affine opens are quasi-compact), and quasi-separated (their diagonals are quasi-compact). Then for every quasi-coherent groupoid module $(M,\alpha)$ there exist a small nonempty filtered category $I$ and a diagram $(M_j,\alpha_j)$ of coherent groupoid modules, with an equivariant cocone to $(M,\alpha)$ exhibiting it as the colimit in the category of quasi-coherent groupoid modules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The morphisms of this diagram are not required to be monomorphisms. All sizes are taken in a universe containing these schemes, modules and indexing categories.

proof.text: Let $I$ be the poset of coherent quasi-coherent submodules $H\subseteq M$, represented by actual subsheaves in the chosen universe. This is a set: each subsheaf is a compatible family of subsets of the sets $M(W)$ indexed by the set of opens. It is nonempty because it contains zero. If $H,K\in I$, their sum is the image of $H\oplus K\to M$. This image is quasi-coherent by the cited image theorem. Its kernel is quasi-coherent by the kernel theorem, so the coherent subquotient theorem applied to $H\oplus K$ makes the image coherent. Thus $H+K\in I$ is an upper bound. A poset has at most one parallel arrow, so $I$ is a small nonempty filtered category.

source.place: Tag 07TU (lemma-colimit-coherent), proof; using the section case in Tag 07TT (lemma-push-pull).

proof.text: The inclusion cocone $(H\hookrightarrow M)_{H\in I}$ is a colimit in module sheaves. Indeed every local section of $M$ lies in some coherent submodule by the section-carrier lemma, applicable because $U$ is Noetherian. A compatible family of maps from the $H$ to any module sheaf $N$ defines its map on a section $m$ by choosing a carrier $H$ and applying that map. Two choices agree in $H+K$; restriction agrees by the same argument. This constructs the unique module map $M\to N$ factoring the cocone.

source.place: Tag 07TU (lemma-colimit-coherent), proof; using the section case in Tag 07TT (lemma-push-pull).

proof.text: Apply the coinduction theorem: write $G(H)=(s_*t^*H,\alpha_H)$ and use the specified equivariant unit $\eta:(M,\beta)\to G(M)$. All its hypotheses hold for the given $s,t$. In the abelian groupoid-module category form $P_H=(M,\beta)\times_{G(M)}G(H)$. The structural theorem computes this as the underlying module pullback. The right adjoint $G$ sends $H\hookrightarrow M$ to a monomorphism: by its adjunction, equality of two maps after $G(H)\to G(M)$ is equality after $H\hookrightarrow M$ of their adjoint maps. Consequently $P_H\to M$ is monic. Inclusions $H\subseteq K$ induce compatible maps $P_H\to P_K$ by the pullback universal property.

source.place: Tag 07TU (lemma-colimit-coherent), proof; using the section case in Tag 07TT (lemma-push-pull).

proof.text: We check coherence directly using the identity section $e$, rather than invoking the general faithfully flat descent case of Tag 07TT. For any quasi-coherent $H$, let $\varepsilon_H:s_*t^*H\to H$ be evaluation along $e$: pull back the ordinary adjunction counit $s^*s_*t^*H\to t^*H$ by $e$ and identify $(s e)^*=\mathrm{id}$ and $(t e)^*=\mathrm{id}$. This is natural in $H$. The specified formula for $\eta$ gives $\varepsilon_M\eta=\mathrm{id}_M$: evaluation of the ordinary unit is the identity, and $e^*\beta^{-1}=1$. If $p_H:P_H\to M$ and $q_H:P_H\to G(H)$ are the pullback maps and $h:H\hookrightarrow M$, naturality gives $h\varepsilon_Hq_H=\varepsilon_M G(h)q_H=\varepsilon_M\eta p_H=p_H$. Thus $\varepsilon_Hq_H:P_H\to H$ is monic since $p_H$ is monic. The structural theorem says $P_H$ is quasi-coherent; hence it is a coherent quasi-coherent submodule of coherent $H$ by the cited submodule theorem.

source.place: Tag 07TU (lemma-colimit-coherent), proof; using the section case in Tag 07TT (lemma-push-pull).

proof.text: Pullback $t^*$ commutes with the colimit of step 2 because it is left adjoint to ordinary module pushforward: a map out of the pulled-back cocone is, by adjunction, exactly a compatible family of maps out of the original cocone. The Zariski continuity theorem applies to $s$ because it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Therefore the canonical comparison $\operatorname{colim}_{H\in I}s_*t^*H\xrightarrow{\sim}s_*t^*M$ is an isomorphism. This is filtered continuity; no assertion about arbitrary colimits of $s_*$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 07TU (lemma-colimit-coherent), proof; using the section case in Tag 07TT (lemma-push-pull).

proof.text: The inclusions $p_H:P_H\hookrightarrow M$ exhaust $M$ on every affine open $W\subseteq U$. For $m\in M(W)$, step 5 and the cited affine-section colimit theorem, applied to the quasi-coherent modules $VG(H)$ supplied by coinduction, give some $H$ and $g\in(s_*t^*H)(W)$ whose image is $\eta(m)$. The pair $(m,g)$ is a section of the module pullback $P_H$ on $W$ and maps to $m$. Compatible maps $P_H\to N$ therefore define a map on every section of $M$ over each affine open. Two choices agree after passing to a common upper bound in $I$, since $P_K\hookrightarrow M$ is monic. Restrictions agree by the same argument on affine opens inside an intersection. These maps glue uniquely to a module-sheaf map $M\to N$. Thus $M$ is the module-sheaf colimit of the $P_H$. The structural theorem makes the equivariant cocone a colimit in the groupoid-module category. Step 4 makes every $P_H$ coherent, proving the assertion (with monic transition maps, which are allowed).

The item statement is unchanged and matches 07TU hypothesis by hypothesis: U and R Noetherian; s, t flat, qc, qs. The variance of the 03LI cocycle is checked. Step 1: I is a set and is directed by H+K, which is coherent via the image/kernel nodes and kernel-cokernel-locnoeth (1),(2). Step 2: the section-carrier holds for every open of the Noetherian U, so the inclusion cocone is a colimit; the tool_use is accepted. Step 3: the right adjoint G preserves monos and P_H is the underlying pullback. Step 4: I verified eps_M eta = id from the triangle identity and e*beta = 1. This gives h eps_H q_H = p_H, so P_H embeds in H and is coherent by locnoeth (2). This is the explicit section case of 07TT with sigma = e. Step 5: t* is a left adjoint and the filtered continuity of s_* gives colim s_*t*H = s_*t*M. Step 6: the affine-section colimit node gives exhaustion and the structural node lifts the colimit to the groupoid category. proof_deps equals the union of uses, and no SGA is cited. The three new nodes are true, self-contained and statement-only, and none restates the item. They were tested on empty U, the trivial groupoid, a group scheme over a field and f = id or empty X. rg -L for the tags and concepts found no duplicates; the nearest hits are descent-tensor-cokernel, coproduct-epi, the etale filtered colimit and space qcoh colimits.
